messages:
jamie.s: Quick announcement: We're deprecating long-lived GitHub PATs in CI workflows and moving to OIDC / GitHub Apps + short-lived creds. Goals: eliminate plaintext secrets in repos, automatic rotation, and smaller blast radius. Rollout schedule: docs & migration tooling by 2026-04-01, audit-only enforcement starting 2026-05-15, hard-block on legacy PATs in workflows 2026-05-30. Post here if you need help.

maria: Do self-hosted runners need changes?

jamie.s: Yes. Self-hosted runners must support OIDC token exchange or use a GitHub App. If you're assuming cloud roles from runners (AWS/GCP/Azure), switch to the OIDC trust flow. We'll publish a runner checklist and sample policies.

sam_k: Service accounts/bots currently use PATs stored in Vault. Recommended approach?

jamie.s: Replace with GitHub App installations or use OIDC-based role assumption. We built a Vault adapter that can mint short-lived tokens via a GitHub App; migration tool will create PRs that update code to call the adapter instead of reading PATs.

diana: Local dev tokens—will devs be forced to stop using personal PATs?

jamie.s: Personal PATs for interactive development remain allowed, but prefer short-lived tokens via `gh auth login` or `gh auth refresh`. Org enforcement targets CI/workflow secrets and org-level secrets.

maria-devex: Devex added a detection script: `./tools/find_pat_usage.sh` — run from repo root. It flags `.github/workflows`, repo secrets, and obvious inline usages. We'll iterate on false positives.

jamie.s: Short migration checklist: - 1) Configure OIDC trust in your cloud account and create a role for GitHub OIDC. - 2) Update workflows: set `permissions: id-token: write` and use an OIDC-capable action to mint creds. Example: 
```
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
steps:
- uses: actions/checkout@v3
- name: Configure AWS via OIDC
  uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
  with:
    role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/GitHubActionsRole
    aws-region: us-west-2
```
- 3) Remove PATs from repo secrets and switch scripts to call the short-lived accessor or use `gh` to fetch tokens. - 4) Run the migration tool which can propose PRs.

sam_k: Can we bulk-migrate hundreds of repos?

jamie.s: Yes. Migration tool supports batching and will open PRs in target repos, but it needs repo admin consent for installs. Devex will coordinate batches and outreach.

ops-bot: Automated notice: migration-checker scheduled weekly. Next run 2026-03-30 02:00 UTC. Reports posted to #eng-security; critical findings will open tickets.

maria: What does the enforcement window look like?

jamie.s: Enforcement timeline: 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-29 = audit-only notifications to owners. 2026-05-30 = start blocking legacy PAT usage in workflows. If you see failures, check Console -> Tools -> Auth -> OIDC token exchange logs.

diana: Will there be docs and office hours?

jamie.s: Docs: https://intranet.redwood.ai/docs/github-oidc-migration (checklist, sample workflows, self-hosted runner guide). Office hours: Tue/Thu 09:00-10:30 PT starting 2026-03-28 in #devex-help. Book a 1:1 if you need help.

maria-devex: We're also adding an auto-PR generator that applies minimal changes (`permissions`, action snippet, README note). PR template will show migration steps and a CI badge.

sam_k: If we hit permission issues installing the org app, who to contact?

jamie.s: Ping @jamie.s and @maria or open ENGSEC ticket. We'll escalate to GitHub if needed.

maria: We'll run the checker across platform/* tomorrow and post findings.

ops-bot: Ticket created: ENGSEC-4821 "OIDC migration batch: platform/*" assigned to devex.

diana: :thumbsup: thanks all.

maria: Thanks, team. We'll post progress here.
